Looking at this problem, I need to find all primes $p, q$ and integers $n$ with $p(p+3)+q(q+3)=n(n+3)$.

**Answer-leak check:** The problem text contains no solutions, proof sketches, or formalization notes. Proceeding.

---

## Setup via completing the square

Multiply by 4 and complete the square. Let $a = 2p+3$, $b = 2q+3$, $c = 2n+3$. Then:

$$a^2 + b^2 = c^2 + 9 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a^2 + b^2 - c^2 = 9.$$

Here $a, b, c$ are all odd, with $a = 2p+3 \ge 7$, $b = 2q+3 \ge 7$.

## Key constraint mod 3

If $p \neq 3$ and $q \neq 3$, then $p, q \equiv \pm 1 \pmod{3}$, so $a = 2p+3 \equiv \pm 2 \pmod{3}$, giving $a^2 \equiv 1 \pmod{3}$; likewise $b^2 \equiv 1 \pmod{3}$. Then

$$c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 9 \equiv 1 + 1 - 0 \equiv 2 \pmod{3},$$

but quadratic residues mod 3 are only $\{0, 1\}$. **Contradiction.** Therefore **at least one of $p, q$ equals $3$.**

## Solving with $p = 3$ (i.e., $a = 9$)

Then $81 + b^2 - 9 = c^2$, i.e., $c^2 - b^2 = 72$, i.e., $(c-b)(c+b) = 72$.

Both $c-b$ and $c+b$ are even (since $b, c$ odd). Write $c - b = d$, $c + b = e$ with $de = 72$, both even, and $b = (e-d)/2 > 0$. Enumerating all even factor pairs $(d, e)$ of $72$:

| $(d, e)$ | $b = (e-d)/2$ | $c = (d+e)/2$ | $q = (b-3)/2$ | valid? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $(2, 36)$ | $17$ | $19$ | $7$ ✓ | $(3,7,8)$ |
| $(4, 18)$ | $7$ | $11$ | $2$ ✓ | $(3,2,4)$ |
| $(6, 12)$ | $3$ | $9$ | $0$ ✗ | not prime |
| $(-36, -2)$ | $17$ | $-19$ | $7$ ✓ | $(3,7,-11)$ |
| $(-18, -4)$ | $7$ | $-11$ | $2$ ✓ | $(3,2,-7)$ |
| $(-12, -6)$ | $3$ | $-9$ | $0$ ✗ | not prime |

All other even pairs give $b \le 0$ (invalid since $b \ge 7$). So with $p = 3$:

$$(3, 7, 8),\quad (3, 7, -11),\quad (3, 2, 4),\quad (3, 2, -7).$$

## By symmetry ($q = 3$)

The equation is symmetric in $p, q$, so swapping gives:

$$(7, 3, 8),\quad (7, 3, -11),\quad (2, 3, 4),\quad (2, 3, -7).$$

The case $p = q = 3$ gives $c^2 = 81 + 81 - 9 = 153$, not a perfect square — no solution.

## The complete set $S$

$$S = \{(2,3,4),\,(2,3,-7),\,(3,2,4),\,(3,2,-7),\,(3,7,8),\,(3,7,-11),\,(7,3,8),\,(7,3,-11)\}.$$

## Computing the sum of $p^2 + q^2 + n^2$

| Triple | $p^2+q^2+n^2$ |
|---|---|
| $(2, 3, 4)$ | $4+9+16 = 29$ |
| $(2, 3, -7)$ | $4+9+49 = 62$ |
| $(3, 2, 4)$ | $9+4+16 = 29$ |
| $(3, 2, -7)$ | $9+4+49 = 62$ |
| $(3, 7, 8)$ | $9+49+64 = 122$ |
| $(3, 7, -11)$ | $9+49+121 = 179$ |
| $(7, 3, 8)$ | $49+9+64 = 122$ |
| $(7, 3, -11)$ | $49+9+121 = 179$ |

$$\text{Sum} = 2(29 + 62 + 122 + 179) = 2 \cdot 392 = \boxed{784}.$$
